standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the reduction of the existence of all finite limits to the existence of finite products and of equalizers.

core_obligations: Finite limits (proof lines 907-913): after citing the reduction to finite products and equalizers, the author notes that finite products exist by the definition of an abelian category and that the equalizer of two parallel morphisms is the kernel of their difference, which exists as well.
Finite colimits (proof line 914): the corresponding statement for finite colimits is dual.
proof_roadmap: Reduce finite limits to finite products and equalizers.
Identify the equalizer with the kernel of the difference and conclude.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that every abelian category has all finite limits and all finite colimits (statement lines 901-905). The proof is a complete argument: the existence of finite limits is reduced, through a named criterion, to finite products, which exist by definition, and to equalizers, which are identified with the kernel of the difference of the two morphisms and hence exist (proof lines 907-913); the statement for finite colimits is dual (proof line 914). The non-formal content is the identification of equalizers with kernels. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
